articles.title: Nick Kyrgios, suspended after testing positive for cocaine: "Nothing justifies what I did"
articles.standfirst: Benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, was detected
articles.summary: Benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, was detected
articles.body:
Nick Kyrgios (31 years old) has been provisionally suspended after testing positive for cocaine.

The BBC reports that the Australian tennis player provided a sample during the Mallorca Open on June 22, in which benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, was later detected.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) reported that Kyrgios, who was once ranked world number 13, had the right to appeal the provisional suspension, "but he has not done so to date".

Cocaine is classified as a stimulant and substance of abuse on the World Anti-Doping Agency's list of prohibited substances.

With this suspension Kyrgios cannot play, train, or attend Grand Slam tournaments or any event sanctioned by the men's and women's tennis tours.

The Australian has only played four singles matches this season, after dealing with knee and wrist injuries in recent years.

Nick Kyrgios, who in Mallorca lost in the first round to Adam Walton, turned to his Instagram account to share a statement in which he acknowledges his guilt, "none of that justifies what I did," and in which he accepts "full responsibility."

"My body has not been able to do what my mind expected of it," shares Kyrgios, who acknowledges that the injuries had taken "an enormous toll, both mentally and physically."

"Accepting that I am close to the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined," he stressed.

Kyrgios announced that he would step away from social media and public life for the next 28 days to "focus on recovering."

articles.title: Medvedev smashes LED screen after losing his cool in Cincinnati
articles.summary: Daniil Medvedev completely lost his cool in Cincinnati, and one unlucky LED screen paid the price.
articles.body:
Daniil Medvedev completely lost his cool in Cincinnati, and one unlucky LED screen paid the price.

During his third-round match against Brandon Nakashima, Medvedev let a ball go thinking the point was over, only for it to bounce back and hit him in the head.

His reaction was immediate. The Russian launched his racket into the LED advertising board behind the court, damaging the screen.

And the frustration didn't stop there. Medvedev later kicked another courtside screen and knocked over microphones as the match slipped away. He received a code violation during the outburst.

Nakashima saved three match points before completing a 6-7, 7-6, 6-1 comeback victory and eliminating Medvedev from Cincinnati.

articles.title: Serena Williams’ fierce return draws gasps after ball flies straight at opponent’s face
articles.summary: The Williams sisters’ doubles comeback in Cincinnati ended in defeat to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns, but Serena Williams still delivered one of the most talked-about moments of the match. During one exchange, Serena’s shot came directly toward her opponent’s face. She immediately apologized, making it appear the hit was completely unintentional. The return was so quick, however, that there was barely any time to react, and the ball struck her opponent before she could move out of the way. The impact was strong enough to send her body backward from the force, almost making her lose her balance.

articles.title: Alcaraz's wrist is already healed: he returns to the courts at the US Open 138 days later
articles.standfirst: Carlitos feels ready to compete in the last major after the on-court tests carried out this week in Murcia
articles.summary: Carlitos feels ready to compete in the last major after the on-court tests carried out this week in Murcia
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz , world number three at 23 years old, sees the light at the end of the tunnel . After an inactivity period that will have stretched to 138 days , the seven-time major champion has recovered from the injury to his right wrist that occurred on April 14 in the first round of the Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell against Otto Virtanen .

Alcaraz, whose initial objective was to return on August 13 at the Cincinnati Masters 1000, decided to stay in Spain and continue training . Embarking on the American venture without being able to strike the ball with full confidence would have been premature.

The tennis player added a compression sleeve to his right arm to feel more secure when hitting . It was not the first time he had opted for that solution. In the spring of 2024 he also wore the sleeve during the clay-court swing after injuring his forearm in his first training session in Monte Carlo .

The real test came this week by recreating the conditions of the United States Open during sessions with Holger Rune , which ended up lasting as long as four hours. This Thursday was the definitive test that convinced Carlitos and his team that he is fit to return to official competition . This very afternoon, he made his return official through his social media with a forceful message: "Here we go" (here we go).

Alcaraz will already be in New York at the beginning of next week to carry out top-level training with the rest of the participants in the last major. It remains to be seen whether he will sign up for the mixed doubles. The organizers, led by Craig Tiley, are keeping one of the three remaining wild cards for him .

The tennis player from El Palmar will thus be able to aim to retain the champion's crown, which is worth 2,000 points. During his absence, he has been unable to defend a total of 6,130 points. Jannik Sinner, his great rival, remains doubtful due to his knee discomfort.

Seven tournaments guaranteed until the end of the season ​

Alcaraz, who withdrew in the round of 16 at the Godó and then missed the Mutua Madrid Open, Rome, Roland Garros, Queen"s, Wimbledon, Montreal and Cincinnati , will play a total of seven tournaments until the end of the season. His official return will be at the US Open (August 30 to September 13);

After that he will be at the Laver Cup (25 to 27); Tokyo (September 30 to October 6); Shanghai (October 7 to 18); Six Kings Slam (October 21 to 24); Paris (November 2 to 8) and the ATP Finals in Turin (November 15 to 22). He would add the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna to his roadmap if Spain defeats Chile away from home on September 19 and 20.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner confirms his withdrawal from the US Open: "I am very sad and disappointed"
articles.standfirst: The Italian has announced on social media that "I still need more time to recover from my right knee problem"
articles.summary: The Italian has announced on social media that "I still need more time to recover from my right knee problem"
articles.body:
Jannik Sinner announced this Friday that he will not play in the upcoming US Open due to physical problems. The Italian, who underwent several medical examinations at the beginning of August to determine whether he would arrive in optimal condition for the last Grand Slam of the year , has confirmed that he will not be in the singles draw of the New York tournament. "Although I have been working hard with my team and medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete in this year's US Open," he said on his social media.

Although I have been working hard with my team and medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete in this year's US Open

Sinner, who has not played any matches since being crowned Wimbledon champion for the second consecutive year, explained that "we have returned to the court in Monte Carlo over the last few days and realized that I still need more time to recover from my right knee problem". The Italian had already withdrawn from the Masters 1000 events in Montreal and Cincinnati.

His definitive absence comes one day after Carlos Alcaraz announced his return four months later. The Spaniard has been away from the courts due to a right wrist injury he suffered in April, during the Conde de Godó tournament in Barcelona.

We've been back on court in Monte Carlo in recent days and we've realized that I still need more time to recover from my right knee problem

The Italian appeared saddened by his absence from the last Grand Slam of the season: "Obviously I am very sad and disappointed, as New York holds a special place in my heart. I was very excited to return and play in the electrifying atmosphere in front of the great fans there".

articles.title: Cincinnati Masters 2026 Prize Money: How much money are this year's winners getting?
articles.standfirst: The Cincinnati Open has a bumper purse on offer as the ATP Masters 1000 event provides a major payday ahead of the US Open
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Open has a bumper purse on offer as the ATP Masters 1000 event provides a major payday ahead of the US Open
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Masters 2026 is offering another substantial financial incentive for the world's leading tennis players, with the men's ATP Masters 1000 tournament carrying a total prize pool of $9,415,725.

The winner of the men's singles competition will take home $1,151,380, while the runner-up is guaranteed $612,340. That means the champion will earn almost twice as much as the player who finishes second, adding another significant reward to the 1,000 ATP ranking points available for lifting the trophy.

The Cincinnati Open is taking place at the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason, Ohio, from August 13-23.

It is the final ATP Masters 1000 tournament before the US Open, making it an important opportunity for players to build momentum, and bank substantial earnings, before the year's final Grand Slam.

The 2026 tournament has also arrived with an expanded format and upgraded facilities following a major renovation of the venue. The event was named ATP Masters 1000 Tournament of the Year at the 2025 ATP Awards, highlighting its growing importance on the calendar.

How much does each round of the Cincinnati Masters pay?

The financial rewards begin well before the final.

A player reaching the second round of the 96-player men's singles draw receives $36,110, while making the third round guarantees $61,865. From there, the payouts increase sharply as players move into the latter stages.

Cincinnati Masters 2026 prize money by round

The figures show why simply reaching the main draw can be financially meaningful for players outside the established elite. A first-round exit still comes with $24,335, while a run to the last 16 pushes earnings beyond the $100,000 mark.

There is also a major difference between prize money and the broader financial rewards associated with a successful Masters 1000 campaign. Players collect ranking points, gain exposure and can potentially benefit from additional bonuses and sponsorship opportunities.

The ATP has been increasing player compensation across its premier events. The tour said that its Masters 1000 profit-sharing model distributed $18.3 million to 186 players in 2025, representing a 25% increase in base Masters 1000 prize money. For 2026, the ATP has also made $21.5 million available through its Masters 1000 and ATP Finals Bonus Pool.

Cincinnati prize money compared with last year

The 2026 men's singles winner's cheque is also larger than it was in 2025.

The Cincinnati Open 's own 2026 compendium lists the men's singles prize money at $9,415,725, compared with $9,193,540 in 2025. The champion's prize has risen from $1,124,380 to $1,151,380, an increase of $27,000.

That increase comes at a particularly interesting moment for the tournament. Several of the sport's biggest names are missing, including 2024 champion Jannik Sinner , who withdrew with a right knee problem, while Carlos Alcaraz is also absent as he continues his recovery from a wrist injury.

As a result, the Cincinnati title is more open than it might have been with the world's top two players in the field. Alexander Zverev entered as the top seed, while Novak Djokovic was among the other major contenders.

For whoever ultimately wins in Ohio, however, the reward is clear: $1.15 million in prize money, 1,000 ranking points and a valuable confidence boost immediately before the US Open.

With the tournament approaching its conclusion on August 23, the remaining players are competing for far more than a trophy.

The Cincinnati Masters has become one of the most lucrative stops on the hard-court calendar, and this year's champion will leave Ohio with one of the biggest paydays available outside the Grand Slams.

articles.title: Coco Gauff blushes after hilarious message to Cincinnati crowd following dominant win
articles.summary: Coco Gauff had already given the Cincinnati crowd plenty to celebrate. Then, after beating Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-2 to reach the semifinals, one fan helped produce one of the sweetest moments of the night.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff had already given the Cincinnati crowd plenty to celebrate. Then, after beating Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-2 to reach the semifinals, one fan helped produce one of the sweetest moments of the night.

During her on-court interview, Gauff remembered hearing someone in the stands shouting, “I’m in love with the Coco,” and couldn't resist bringing it up.

“I don’t know who was saying ‘I’m in love with the Coco,’ but I like that one. That was a good one. And it’s the right Coco!” she joked.

The crowd immediately erupted, and Gauff's reaction made the moment even better. The 22-year-old smiled, covered part of her face and appeared to blush as the cheers and noise grew around her.

articles.title: Coco Gauff blushes and can’t hide her reaction after Cincinnati crowd sends her an unexpected message
articles.standfirst: The 22-year-old dominated Marta Kostyuk to reach the semifinals, but it was what happened afterward that finally left her looking uncomfortable
articles.summary: The 22-year-old dominated Marta Kostyuk to reach the semifinals, but it was what happened afterward that finally left her looking uncomfortable
articles.body:
Coco Gauff spent barely more than an hour looking completely in control against Marta Kostyuk . It took the Cincinnati crowd only a few seconds to make her lose her composure. Not because of anything negative. Quite the opposite.

After cruising past Kostyuk 6-2, 6-2 in just 68 minutes to reach the Cincinnati Open semifinals , Gauff was asked during her on-court interview what made playing in front of the American crowd special. That's when she remembered something she had been hearing from the stands.

“I don’t know who was saying ‘I’m in love with Coco,’ but I like that one. That was a good one,” Gauff said before adding with a smile: “And it’s the right Coco!” The response was immediate.

Fans erupted around the court, and suddenly the player who had handled almost everything Kostyuk threw at her didn't quite know what to do with all the attention. Gauff smiled, brought her hands toward her face and appeared to blush while the crowd continued cheering.

Coco Gauff gave Cincinnati plenty to celebrate

The American broke Kostyuk six times and won 62 of the match's 103 total points . Gauff won 78% of the points behind her first serve and committed only three double faults, while Kostyuk struggled with eight double faults and 38 unforced errors.

The 6-2, 6-2 victory also sent Gauff into her fifth WTA 1000 semifinal of the 2026 season and kept alive her chance of winning Cincinnati for a second time after her breakthrough title there in 2023. She will face Czech surprise Sara Bejlek for a place in the final.

Her run has become increasingly convincing. After needing three sets to get past Liudmila Samsonova in her opening match, Gauff defeated Ann Li, Marie Bouzkova and now Kostyuk on her way to the final four . Against Bouzkova she won 6-3, 6-2 before producing an even more dominant performance in the quarterfinals.

Gauff will now face 20-year-old Czech Sara Bejlek in the semifinals, in what will be the first career meeting between the two. Bejlek has been one of Cincinnati's biggest surprises, knocking out world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in straight sets before coming from behind to defeat former US Open champion Madison Keys 3-6, 6-4, 7-6(5) in the quarterfinals.

The unseeded World No. 35 is playing the first WTA 1000 semifinal of her career, while Gauff is chasing a second Cincinnati title after winning the tournament in 2023.

articles.title: Cincinnati Masters Winners: Complete list of winners in every category
articles.standfirst: From Roger Federer and Serena Williams to Novak Djokovic and Coco Gauff, here is a look at the champions who have lifted Cincinnati’s trophies
articles.summary: From Roger Federer and Serena Williams to Novak Djokovic and Coco Gauff, here is a look at the champions who have lifted Cincinnati’s trophies
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Open , historically known as the Cincinnati Masters , has one of the deepest histories on the professional tennis calendar.

Dating back to 1899, the tournament has produced champions from several generations of the sport, with legends such as Roger Federer, Serena Williams, Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal all among its winners.

The event has also evolved considerably over the decades. Today, the Cincinnati Open is one of the most important ATP Masters 1000 and WTA 1000 tournaments, traditionally serving as a major preparation event for the US Open.

The tournament's official records list champions across four principal categories: men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles and women's doubles.

The history stretches back more than 125 years, although the women's competition and the various doubles events have not been contested continuously throughout that entire period.

For the modern era, Cincinnati has become a particularly prestigious stop on the hard-court calendar. Winning there often provides an important confidence boost heading into the final Grand Slam of the season.

Recent Cincinnati Open champions

The most recent champions before the 2026 tournament illustrate the quality of players who have succeeded in Ohio.

In 2025, Carlos Alcaraz won the men's singles title, while Iga Swiatek claimed the women's singles championship.

The doubles titles went to Nikola Mektic and Rajeev Ram in the men's competition and Gabriela Dabrowski and Erin Routliffe in the women's draw.

The previous year saw Jannik Sinner and Aryna Sabalenka take the singles trophies. Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic won the men's doubles title, while Asia Muhammad and Erin Routliffe triumphed in women's doubles.

The 2023 edition was particularly memorable because Novak Djokovic defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the men's final, while Coco Gauff won the women's singles title.

The doubles champions were Maximo Gonzalez and Andres Molteni on the men's side, with Alycia Parks and Taylor Townsend taking the women's crown.

Cincinnati Masters winners by year

Here is the recent list of champions in the four main categories:

2025: Men's singles — Carlos Alcaraz; women's singles — Iga Swiatek; men's doubles — Nikola Mektic/Rajeev Ram; women's doubles — Gabriela Dabrowski/Erin Routliffe.

2024: Men's singles — Jannik Sinner; women's singles — Aryna Sabalenka; men's doubles — Marcelo Arevalo/Mate Pavic; women's doubles — Asia Muhammad/Erin Routliffe.

2023: Men's singles — Novak Djokovic; women's singles — Coco Gauff; men's doubles — Maximo Gonzalez/Andres Molteni; women's doubles — Alycia Parks/Taylor Townsend.

2022: Men's singles — Borna Coric; women's singles — Caroline Garcia; men's doubles — Rajeev Ram/Joe Salisbury; women's doubles — Lyudmyla Kichenok/Jelena Ostapenko.

articles.title: Anna Wintour steals the spotlight at US Open with a very Vogue family arrival
articles.standfirst: The fashion icon arrived at Arthur Ashe Stadium alongside daughter Bee Shaffer and daughter-in-law Elizabeth Cordry for a special night of tennis
articles.summary: The fashion icon arrived at Arthur Ashe Stadium alongside daughter Bee Shaffer and daughter-in-law Elizabeth Cordry for a special night of tennis
articles.body:
A nna Wintour knows how to make an entrance , even when the runway happens to lead into a tennis stadium.

The fashion icon arrived at the US Open alongside her daughter Bee Shaffer and daughter-in-law Elizabeth Cordry , turning a simple walk into Arthur Ashe Stadium into an unmistakably stylish family moment.

The three women leaned into polished, coordinated looks without dressing identically. Wintour, instantly recognizable behind her signature sunglasses, walked between Bee and Elizabeth as cameras captured the trio arriving together for one of the biggest nights of US Open Fan Week.

Anna Wintour makes the US Open a family affair

Bee, 39, is Wintour's daughter with her late former husband David Shaffer and has built much of her career away from her mother's fashion empire, working in television and theater production. Elizabeth is married to Wintour's son Charles Shaffer, making their appearance together a rare glimpse of the family surrounding one of fashion's most recognizable figures.

The three have shared the spotlight before. Wintour, Bee and Elizabeth were also photographed together earlier this year at the New York premiere of The Devil Wears Prada 2, where Wintour's unmistakable influence on the world of fashion made their family appearance particularly fitting.

This time, however, tennis provided the backdrop. Wintour was at Arthur Ashe Stadium for Roger Federer: An Icon Returns to New York , a special exhibition featuring the 20-time Grand Slam champion alongside fellow tennis legends Andre Agassi, Andy Roddick and John McEnroe.

The night ultimately belonged to Federer. Back on Arthur Ashe for the first time since his final US Open appearance in 2019, the 45-year-old showed flashes of the brilliance that once made him nearly unbeatable in New York, defeating longtime rival and friend Roddick 6-3 in a one-set exhibition before teaming up with McEnroe for doubles against Roddick and Agassi.

Afterward, Federer addressed the packed stadium during an emotional return to the court where he won five consecutive US Open titles. "It's great to be back in New York," he told the crowd as he reflected on his memories at the tournament and in the city.

The moment carried even greater meaning because Federer never had a proper US Open farewell after his final appearance in 2019, making this return an opportunity to finally thank New York and say goodbye on his own terms.

For Wintour, a longtime tennis fan and close friend of Federer, being at Arthur Ashe was hardly surprising. What made the entrance stand out was having Bee and Elizabeth at her side.
